name: Finland

facts.religion: Lutheran about 63% (church members), no religion about 33%

snapshot: NATO's newest frontline state, which joined in 2023 after decades of neutrality, now led by a right-wing coalition cutting spending as unemployment rises.
culture: Finland has more saunas than cars, and sauna culture is UNESCO-listed. Its design heritage, from Marimekko and Alvar Aalto to Nokia and Angry Birds, is famous. The Sámi people of Lapland have their own languages and reindeer herding traditions. Finns prize sisu, a stubborn perseverance, and silence is socially comfortable.
society: Finland regularly tops world happiness rankings and has a celebrated school system. Its 1,340-kilometre border with Russia, now closed, shapes security policy, and it maintains large reserves through conscription. The economy has stagnated since Nokia's phone business collapsed, and unemployment is among the EU's highest.
situation: Petteri Orpo's National Coalition leads a coalition with the nationalist Finns Party that has cut benefits and spending. Alexander Stubb, a former prime minister, won the presidency in 2024 and has become a prominent voice on Ukraine and a golf partner of Trump. The next parliamentary election is due in April 2027.
power: A parliamentary republic. The prime minister leads a majority coalition in the 200-seat Eduskunta; the directly elected president leads foreign and security policy together with the government.
